'''John Kuriyan''' is an American structural biologist and biochemist. He is the dean of basic sciences and a professor of biochemistry at [[Vanderbilt University School of Medicine]]. He was previously a professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and an investigator of the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]]. He was elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] in 2001 and to the [[National Academy of Medicine]] in 2018.

==Education==
Kuriyan received his B.S. in chemistry from [[Juniata College]] in Pennsylvania, followed by his Ph.D. in physical chemistry at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] supervised by [[Gregory Petsko]] and [[Martin Karplus]].<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=The structure and flexibility of myoglobin: molecular dynamics and x-ray crystallography|date=1986|language=en|first=John|last=Kuriyan|oclc=15862419}}</ref>

==Research and career==
Kuriyan did [[postdoctoral research]] for one year with [[Martin Karplus]] at [[Harvard University]] before becoming an assistant professor at [[Rockefeller University]].<ref name="Winstepforward">{{cite web |title=John Kuriyan |url=https://www.winstepforward.org/mentor/john-kuriyan/ |website=WinStep Forward |access-date=2026-04-04}}</ref><ref name="HHMI">{{cite web |title=John Kuriyan |url=https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/john-kuriyan |website=Howard Hughes Medical Institute |access-date=2026-04-04}}</ref> Kuriyan's laboratory studies the structure and mechanism of enzymes and other proteins involved in cellular signal transduction and [[DNA replication]].<ref name="Winstepforward" /><ref name="HHMI" /><ref name="BSR">{{cite web |last=Torres Vera |first=Héctor L. |title=Faculty Profile: John Kuriyan |url=https://berkeleysciencereview.com/article/2022/12/04/faculty-profile-john-kuriyan |website=Berkeley Science Review |date=2022-12-03 |access-date=2026-04-04}}</ref> 

Kuriyan's research has focused on the structural basis of protein kinase regulation and signaling, including mechanisms of activation and inhibition in tyrosine kinases.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Schindler |first1=T. |last2=Bornmann |first2=W. |last3=Pellicena |first3=P. |last4=Miller |first4=W. T. |last5=Clarkson |first5=B. |last6=Kuriyan |first6=J. |title=Structural mechanism for STI-571 inhibition of abelson tyrosine kinase |journal=Science |year=2000 |volume=289 |issue=5486 |pages=1938–1942 |doi=10.1126/science.289.5486.1938 |pmid=10988075}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zhang |first1=Xuewu |last2=Gureasko |first2=Jodi |last3=Shen |first3=Kui |last4=Cole |first4=Philip A. |last5=Kuriyan |first5=John |title=An allosteric mechanism for activation of the kinase domain of epidermal growth factor receptor |journal=Cell |year=2006 |volume=125 |issue=6 |pages=1137–1149 |doi=10.1016/j.cell.2006.05.013 |pmid=16777603}}</ref> This is based in part on the use [[X-ray crystallography]]. His work has also contributed to methodological advances in macromolecular structure determination, including the use of molecular dynamics in crystallographic refinement.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brünger |first1=Axel T. |last2=Kuriyan |first2=John |last3=Karplus |first3=Martin |title=Crystallographic R factor refinement by molecular dynamics |journal=Science |year=1987 |volume=235 |issue=4787 |pages=458–460 |doi=10.1126/science.235.4787.458 |pmid=17810339}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
In 1989, Kuriyan was named a [[Pew Scholar]]. He received the Schering-Plough Award of the [[American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology]] (1994), the Dupont–Merck Award of the Protein Society (1997), the [[Eli Lilly Award in Biological Chemistry]] of the [[American Chemical Society]] (1998), and the Cornelius Rhoads Memorial Award from the [[American Association for Cancer Research]] (1999).<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=71t5u7j1YoQC|title=Journal of the National Cancer Institute: JNCI|date=May 1999|publisher=U.S. Department of Health, Education, and Welfare, Public Health Service, National Institutes of Health|pages=830|language=en}}</ref> He was awarded the [[Richard Lounsbery Award]] of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nasonline.org/programs/awards/richard-lounsbery-award.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111126043755/http://www.nasonline.org/programs/awards/richard-lounsbery-award.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 26, 2011|title=Richard Lounsbery Award|website=www.nasonline.org|access-date=2020-02-08}}</ref> In 2009 he received the ASBMB Merck Award for his contributions to structural biology. Kuriyan was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society|Foreign Member of the Royal Society]] in 2015.<ref name=formemrs/> He was elected to the [[National Academy of Medicine]] in 2018.<ref>{{cite web |title=National Academy of Medicine Elects 85 New Members |url=https://nam.edu/national-academy-of-medicine-elects-85-new-members/ |website=National Academy of Medicine |access-date=2 May 2019 |date=15 October 2018}}</ref>
